_schema.description: Rule that turns typed input into the country's standard written postal code. Countries come from libaddressinput countryinfo.txt (commit in sources/libaddressinput/COMMIT).
procedure: 1. Remove every character in `strip` from the input (compact form).
3. If the compact form does not fit the pattern after formatting and `prefix.strip_if_typed`, remove a leading prefix (prefix text with `strip` characters removed, case-insensitive) and retry.
4. Apply every op in `insert`. Positions and conditions are evaluated on the compact string, then all characters are inserted at once.
5. The result must fully match the libaddressinput `zip` pattern.

insert_op.after: int n: insert `char` after the n-th character (counted from the start)
insert_op.before_last: int n: insert `char` before the last n characters
insert_op.only_when_length: optional list of compact lengths; op applies only for these lengths
insert_op.only_when_match: optional regex tested (re.search) on the upper-cased compact string; op applies only when it matches

_schema.prefix: null, or {text, status: required|optional, scope, strip_if_typed}. A prefix written on mail in front of the code but NOT part of the libaddressinput pattern; the canonical form excludes it. Letters that the pattern itself contains (AD, BB, LV-, KY, VC, VG...) are part of the code, not a prefix.
_schema.canonical_examples: zipex values in standard form, same order; zipex values that cannot be valid are moved to `invalid_zipex` with a reason.
_schema.zipex_deviations: {zipex: {canonical, reason}} for zipex values whose official written form differs from how libaddressinput writes them.
_schema.extra_examples: typed input -> expected output, from the official source; used for countries without zipex or to test prefixes.
_schema.confidence: high = rule confirmed by `source`; low = not confirmed or pattern conflicts with source (see notes).
_schema.source: UPU addressing document for the country (or the parent operator's document when the UPU page refers to it).

AC.notes: UK-style postcode: one space before the inward code (last 3 characters).

AD.notes: Letters AD are part of the code (UPU: 'AD is a part of the postcode').

AF.notes: No separator. Pattern conflicts with or is not backed by the official source: UPU: 6 digits (100208); pattern/zipex are 4 digits.

prefix.scope: UPU: 'with a dash before the numeric part' (AI-2640)

AI.notes: Prefix is written on mail but is not part of the libaddressinput pattern, so canonical form excludes it.

AM.notes: No separator. Pattern conflicts with or is not backed by the official source: UPU: 4 digits (0002); zipex 375010 is the old Soviet-era 6-digit form, allowed by the pattern '(37)?'.

AR.notes: CPA: 1 letter + 4 digits + 3 letters, no separator (UPU: Y5900FNF). Pattern also accepts the old 4-digit code.

AS.notes: US territory using USPS ZIP codes; pattern allows only the 5-digit ZIP, so no ZIP+4 hyphen.

AX.notes: Prefix is written on mail but is not part of the libaddressinput pattern, so canonical form excludes it.

prefix.scope: UPU: 'ISO country code and 4 digits', no separator (AZ1010 Baku)

AZ.notes: Prefix is written on mail but is not part of the libaddressinput pattern, so canonical form excludes it.

BB.notes: Letters BB are part of the code (UPU: 'preceded by BB', BB26028), no separator.

BD.notes: UPU writes 'DHAKA – 1340': the dash separates locality and code, not part of the code.

BM.notes: UPU: 4 alphanumeric characters with a space between the 2nd and 3rd.

BN.notes: Pattern allows a space after the 2 letters; UPU writes BT2328 without one.

invalid_zipex.20050: 5 digits; Belarus codes are 6 digits (220050 is also listed)

CA.notes: UPU/Canada Post: ANA NAN with a space between 3rd and 4th characters.

CC.notes: UPU: 'See Australia'. No zipex; Australia Post code 6799 used as the test example.

CK.notes: No separator. Pattern conflicts with or is not backed by the official source: UPU Cook Islands document shows no postcode at all; pattern \d{4} has no zipex and no official basis.

CL.notes: UPU coding diagram splits '872 0019' but addresses write 8720019 with no space.

CO.notes: UPU coding diagram splits '11 02 21' but addresses write the 6 digits together.

CR.notes: UPU: 5 digits, no separator. The pattern also allows 4 digits and a 7-digit 'NNN-NNNN' form, whose hyphen rule is not confirmed by the official source.

CX.notes: UPU: 'See Australia'. No zipex; Australia Post code 6798 used as the test example.

prefix.scope: UPU: 'preceded by CY- for inbound mail'; domestic example has none (6036 Larnaka)

CY.notes: Prefix is written on mail but is not part of the libaddressinput pattern, so canonical form excludes it.

CZ.notes: UPU: 5 digits with a space between 3rd and 4th digits. Two spaces between code and locality on mail (not part of the code).

EC.notes: No separator. Pattern conflicts with or is not backed by the official source: UPU: 6 digits (090306), no separator; pattern also allows old alphanumeric forms (H0103C, EC090112).

EG.notes: No separator. Pattern conflicts with or is not backed by the official source: UPU: 7 digits; pattern/zipex are 5 digits.

EH.notes: No UPU document for Western Sahara; addresses use Barid Al-Maghrib 5-digit codes (Morocco document).

FK.notes: UK-style postcode: one space before the inward code (last 3 characters).

FM.notes: US territory using USPS ZIP codes; format from the USA UPU document (territory UPU page only gives the ZIP range).

prefix.scope: UPU: 'ISO code alpha-2 (FO) plus 3 digits' (FO-100 Tórshavn)

FO.notes: Prefix is written on mail but is not part of the libaddressinput pattern, so canonical form excludes it.

FR.notes: Pattern allows a space after 2 digits, but La Poste/UPU write 5 digits without a space (33380).

invalid_zipex.RH6 OHP: letter O where the inward code needs digit 0; the correct 'RH6 0HP' is also listed

GB.notes: UK-style postcode: one space before the inward code (last 3 characters). BFPO codes are written 'BFPO <n>' (space after BFPO). zipex BS18 8HF is a retired district but still matches the pattern.

GG.notes: UK-style postcode: one space before the inward code (last 3 characters).

GI.notes: UK-style postcode: one space before the inward code (last 3 characters). UPU: single generic code GX11 1AA.

GL.notes: UPU: 'See Denmark'; source is the Denmark document.

GN.notes: UPU: 3 digits, often followed by a BP (P.O. box) number, which is not part of the code.

GR.notes: UPU: 5 digits with a space between 3rd and 4th digits.

GS.notes: UK-style postcode: one space before the inward code (last 3 characters).

GU.notes: US territory using USPS ZIP codes; format from the USA UPU document (territory UPU page only gives the ZIP range).

HM.notes: No separator. Pattern conflicts with or is not backed by the official source: Uninhabited (UPU); Australia Post postcode 7151 used for Australian Antarctic/HM mail is not confirmed by the UPU document.

HN.notes: No separator. Pattern conflicts with or is not backed by the official source: UPU: 2 letters + 4 digits (CM1102); pattern is 5 digits with no zipex.

HR.notes: Prefix is written on mail but is not part of the libaddressinput pattern, so canonical form excludes it.

prefix.scope: UPU: 4 digits 'preceded by HT', no separator (HT6120 DELMAS)

HT.notes: Prefix is written on mail but is not part of the libaddressinput pattern, so canonical form excludes it.

IL.notes: UPU: 7 digits (9414219); pattern also accepts the old 5 digits. No separator.

IM.notes: UK-style postcode: one space before the inward code (last 3 characters). UPU Isle of Man page: 'See United Kingdom' (example IM99 1PS); source is the GB document.

IO.notes: UK-style postcode: one space before the inward code (last 3 characters).

IQ.notes: No zipex; UPU example 61002 used as the test example.

11936-12345.reason: UPU Iran document writes the 10-digit code with no separator (1619614153); zipex has a hyphen after the 5th digit

IR.notes: Canonical form follows UPU (10 digits, no separator). Pattern allows an optional hyphen; no official source for the hyphen was found.

JE.notes: UK-style postcode: one space before the inward code (last 3 characters). UPU Jersey page: 'See United Kingdom'; source is the GB document.

KH.notes: No separator. Pattern conflicts with or is not backed by the official source: UPU: 6 digits (120209); pattern/zipex are 5 digits.

KR.notes: Pattern/zipex are the pre-2015 6-digit 'NNN-NNN' format. UPU Korea document: since 1 Aug 2015 the code is 5 digits with no separator (e.g. 42007). The hyphen rule reproduces the old format but is not confirmed by the current official source; codes matching this pattern are obsolete.

KY.notes: UPU: 'KY' + island digit, hyphen, 4 digits (KY1-1100). Letters are part of the code.

KZ.notes: No separator. Pattern conflicts with or is not backed by the official source: UPU: new 7-character alphanumeric code (Z00Y5M3); pattern/zipex are the old 6 digits.

LB.notes: UPU Lebanon document has no postcode section. 8-digit codes are written NNNN NNNN in zipex and in secondary sources; 4-digit codes have no separator. Not confirmed from LibanPost.

LI.notes: UPU: Liechtenstein uses Swiss Post's system; source is the Switzerland document.

prefix.scope: UPU: Lithuania Post requires the ISO country code (LT-04340 Vilnius)

LT.notes: Prefix is written on mail but is not part of the libaddressinput pattern, so canonical form excludes it.

prefix.scope: UPU: 4 digits 'preceded by L' (L-1234 DUDELANGE); the prefix is L, not LU

LU.notes: Prefix is written on mail but is not part of the libaddressinput pattern, so canonical form excludes it.

LV.notes: UPU: 'LV-' + 4 digits; the LV- is part of the libaddressinput pattern, so it is in the canonical form.

MD.notes: Prefix is written on mail but is not part of the libaddressinput pattern, so canonical form excludes it.

MH.notes: US territory using USPS ZIP codes; format from the USA UPU document (territory UPU page only gives the ZIP range).

MT.notes: UPU: 'One space between letters and digits' (ZTN 1073). Old 2-digit codes (NXR 01) in zipex predate the 2007 4-digit scheme but follow the same spacing.

MU.notes: No separator. Pattern conflicts with or is not backed by the official source: UPU: 5 digits (42602), or R + 4 digits for Rodrigues; the pattern only accepts 3 digits + 2 letters + 3 digits (742CU001), which is not in the official source.

NF.notes: UPU: 'Postcode of NORFOLK ISLAND is 2899'. No zipex; 2899 used as the test example.

NL.notes: UPU/PostNL: space between the digits and the 2 capital letters (1234 AB).

prefix.scope: Pattern allows an optional 'PC ' (postal code) label; UPU shows 3 digits only (133)

PE.notes: Pattern/zipex use the old 'LIMA nn' / 'CALLAO n' zones; the space follows the zipex. UPU Peru document: current code is 5 digits with no separator (e.g. 15074), which this rule leaves unchanged.

PF.notes: No zipex; UPU example 98709 used as the test example.

PK.notes: UPU writes 'ISLAMABAD–44000': the dash separates locality and code, not part of the code.

PN.notes: UK-style postcode: one space before the inward code (last 3 characters).

SV.notes: Pattern requires 'CP ' + 4 digits; UPU El Salvador document shows 4 digits only (1120), without CP. The 'CP ' form is kept because the pattern requires it, but it is not confirmed officially.

TA.notes: UK-style postcode: one space before the inward code (last 3 characters).

TC.notes: UK-style postcode: one space before the inward code (last 3 characters).

TW.notes: UPU Taiwan document not available. Pattern allows 3 or 5 digits with no separator, as in zipex. Chunghwa Post now uses 3+3 (6-digit) codes, which this pattern does not accept; the separator for 3+3 is not given on the Chunghwa Post page checked.

TZ.notes: No separator. Pattern conflicts with or is not backed by the official source: UPU: 5 digits (11101); pattern/zipex are 4 digits.

US.notes: UPU/USPS: ZIP+4 written with a hyphen between 5th and 6th digits; 5-digit ZIP has no separator.

VC.notes: Letters VC are part of the code (UPU: VC0120).

VG.notes: Letters VG are part of the code (UPU: VG1110).

VI.notes: US territory using USPS ZIP codes; format from the USA UPU document (territory UPU page only gives the ZIP range).

VN.notes: No separator. Pattern conflicts with or is not backed by the official source: UPU: 5 digits; pattern/zipex are 6 digits.

XK.notes: No UPU document for Kosovo. 5 digits, no separator as in zipex and Kosovo institutional addresses (e.g. 10000 Prishtinë); not confirmed from Posta e Kosovës.

_no_postal_code_notes.IE: No `zip` in this countryinfo.txt snapshot, although Ireland has used Eircode (e.g. A65 F4E2, space after 3rd character) since 2015. Left out because there is no pattern to check against.
